headline: Nvidia stopped selling advanced AI chips to China entirely as Trump's chip crackdown heated up, while Anthropic went public at over $1 trillion and researchers updated AI timelines after a new acceleration report.

points.text: Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China, despite approval it received from the White House in December, interim CEO Colette Kress announced.

The Trump administration's plans to clamp down on China's access to AI chips are heating up, motivated in part by the Nvidia spy scandal, as officials say they doubt Trump's China trip will yield progress on AI.
Anthropic went public, raising over $81 billion in an IPO that valued the Claude maker at over $1 trillion.
Axios and Wired warned of a 'terrifying rise' in widely available AI hacking tools, including one called Artex, that let even unsophisticated attackers breach networks within hours.
The AI Futures Project and a separate newsletter proposed concrete ways to 'pace' frontier AI development through compute reallocation.
Commentators reacted to a new METR report on AI R&D acceleration by updating their AI timelines, including new predictions from Paul Christiano.
The ITU's AI for Good discussed global challenges in making AI telecommunications standards more accessible, and how AI is reshaping the pharmaceutical value chain.
